fact: Wearetech reports that Comores Numérique 2028, the national strategy drawn up in 2018, has been implemented by the national digital development agency ANADEN since 2019.
Al-watwan reports the minister saying ANADEN is to contribute to implementing the Stratégie numérique Comores 2028 across the sectors of the economy.
We Are Tech Africa states the 'Comoros Digital 2028' plan aims to raise the digital sector's share of GDP to 5% by 2028, a dated target with no cost given.

Digital Watch Observatory states Comoros' digital governance is built around the Stratégie Comores Numériques 2028, implemented by ANADEN, and frames digital as a lever for economic development, public-service modernisation and sector reform; the page gives only a 2024 published date, used here.

The Ministry of Health's digital health strategy states that ANADEN was created in 2019 under the Presidency's Secretariat General of the Government, with implementing the 'Comores Numérique 2028' strategy as its first mission.
The digital health strategy says the Government drew up the 'stratégie numérique Comores 2028' in 2018 and refers to its 'adoption' in the same year; it names no adopting act or body.
The strategy's text is public on ANADEN's site, with a baseline year of 2018 and a roadmap running 2018-2028; it prints no publication date and ANADEN dates its drawing-up to December 2018.

The strategy costs its six axes and thirteen orientations at 52,995,160,485 KMF in total, the largest line being complete national broadband coverage at 32,629,410,800 KMF; the figures are planned costings of 2018.

The strategy designs three bodies: a Conseil National sur le Numérique chaired by the Secrétaire général du gouvernement, ANADEN to implement it, and an Observatoire national du numérique to measure sector performance.
